newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS EDGES OUT BECKER IN ATP TOUR FINALE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS EDGES OUT BECKER IN ATP TOUR FINALE.

text.p: Pete Sampras clinched the ATP Tour world championship for the third time when he beat defending champion Boris Becker 3-6 7-6 7-6 6-7 6-4 in a dramatic five-set final on Sunday.
The world number one, winner in 1991 and 1994, battled back from one set behind to defeat the three times Wimbledon champion in front of 15,000 of his fanatical German fans in exactly four hours.
But it required an immense effort from the American. The pair played out an intense fourth-set tiebreak when Becker saved two match points to win 13-11.
The victory was worth $1.34 million to the American who became the fifth player to win the championship, formerly known as the Masters, three or more times.
Becker and John McEnroe have also won the title three times, Ilie Nastase triumphed four times and Ivan Lendl won five championships.
